subject: Multiple data sets in a single scatter plot

messages.author: 04a7abfe7698b6c1
messages.subject: Multiple data sets in a single scatter plot
parts:
Hi,

I am a new ggplot2 user and I have hit a wall with something that
in principle should be relatively easy to do. I would like to generate
a scatter plot using a color coded gradient for the data, over which I
would like to overlay a single point, at coordinates x=0.002652,
y=0.054668, in a different color (say red) to highlight it from the
rest of the set. Here is the code I am currently using which is only
generating the first plot. A working example of how to solve this
challenge would be most appreciated. Thanks so much for your help!

------- code:

library(ggplot2)
pTable <- read.csv("test.csv", header=T)
attach(pTable)
png(filename="test.png" ,width=800, height=600)
p <- qplot(sigma, R,
colour = Z,
data = pTable,
xlab = "sigma",
ylab = "Y",
main = "Title")
p + scale_colour_gradientn(colour = topo.colors(10))
p + geom_point(0.002652,0.054668,colour = "red", size = 3)
dev.off()

messages.author: 40f7d34e9dd27d88
messages.subject: Re: Multiple data sets in a single scatter plot
parts:
hello,

The best way would be to put the point coordinates in an own data.frame

I would do it like this:

point <- data.frame(disp=300,wt=4)
ggplot(mtcars,aes(disp,wt,colour=gear)) + geom_point() +
scale_colour_gradientn(colour = topo.colors(10)) +
geom_point(data=point,size=3,colour="red")

regards,
Stefan
